sections.h2: Bottles, coolers, kayaks and shampoo: the sticker gets wet, the print should not care
sections.html:
Water is the quickest way to kill a sticker. Paper soaks and wrinkles, unprotected ink runs, and the adhesive floats off. A waterproof sticker fixes all three at once: a film base that cannot absorb anything, a laminate over the ink, and an adhesive that bonds to the surface before the water arrives. This page covers that material across every format we print: rectangles and circles, kiss cut sheets, roll labels and shape-cut pieces. The sibling product, the die cut waterproof sticker page, is only the shape-cut version, each sticker trimmed to its artwork outline. If you are after labels for a product line or a sheet of designs rather than individual contour-cut stickers, you are on the right page.

The jobs we see most are water bottle and tumbler stickers, cosmetic and soap labels, cooler and kayak decals, bathroom and kitchen labels, sports gear and anything sold at outdoor markets.

People ask how to print waterproof stickers at home, and the honest answer is that a desktop inkjet on paper will not get there. The job needs the right stock, inks that dry on film, and a laminate. Here is the sequence on our press.

  1. Stock: white vinyl for solid color, clear vinyl or clear BOPP for the no-background look. Neither absorbs water. Paper is never used for this product.
  2. Ink: full-color CMYK and Pantone matches printed with inks that cure on film rather than soaking in, so the image sits on the surface as a dry layer.
  3. Laminate: a clear gloss or matte film pressed over the whole sheet. This is the layer that takes the dishwasher, the sunscreen and the scrubbing, and it is why laminated vinyl outlasts a "water-resistant" coating.
  4. Adhesive: permanent acrylic adhesive by default, which keeps its grip once wet; removable is available for glass and rental gear.
  5. Cut: die cut through the liner for singles, kiss cut for sheets, or roll-wound for applicators. Edges are sealed by the laminate so water has no way in.

sections.h2: Waterproof, water-resistant or all-weather: the words are not the same
sections.html:
Shops use these terms loosely. Here is how we mean them, so you can order the right thing.

Most buyers need the middle row. If the sticker will sit on a truck, a sign or a mailbox through summers and winters, move up a row; the materials on the feature-based sticker categories include the outdoor and reflective films built for that.

sections.h2: Surfaces that work, and the ones that fight back
sections.html:
Waterproof means the sticker itself survives water. The bond to the surface is a separate question, and some surfaces are hard on any adhesive.

  • Stainless and glass bottles: ideal. Clean with rubbing alcohol first, apply dry, press for 30 seconds.
  • Hard plastics (coolers, kayaks, cases): good with permanent adhesive; polyethylene coolers are low-energy plastics, so let the sticker set 24 hours before it gets wet.
  • Painted metal and fiberglass: good. Avoid fresh paint that has not cured.
  • Tile and ceramic: good on glazed surfaces, poor on unglazed or textured tile.
  • Silicone, rubber and soft-touch coatings: poor. Adhesive peels within days no matter how waterproof the sticker is.
  • Powder-coated tumblers: fine for the film, but the texture lowers the grip, so keep stickers under 3" and press firmly.

Rinse off sunscreen and insect repellent when you can; both are solvents and will haze a laminate over a season.

sections.h2: Permanent or removable adhesive when the surface gets wet
sections.html: Permanent adhesive is the default for waterproof stickers because it is the one that keeps holding once water gets to the edge. It suits bottles, gear, boats and product labels that stay on for the life of the item. Removable adhesive lets the sticker come off glass, steel and smooth plastic clean, which is right for rental equipment, seasonal labels on reusable containers and shop windows, but it tolerates fewer wet cycles before the edges start to lift. If you need a sticker that comes off and goes back on repeatedly, that is a different construction, and our custom reusable sticker range covers the restickable and static cling options.

sections.h2: Ordering, dishwashers and the questions that come up every week
sections.html:
Top-rack dishwasher cycles are fine for laminated vinyl on a steel or glass bottle; months of daily washes will eventually dull the gloss, so order matte laminate if the bottle gets washed every day. Freezer use is fine if the sticker goes on at room temperature. Salt water is fine for the film; rinse the surface afterward so salt does not creep under the edge. Hot tubs and pool chemicals are the one thing we warn about, since chlorine attacks the adhesive over time.

To order, send a vector file or a 300 dpi image at final size, choose white or clear film, gloss or matte laminate, and permanent or removable adhesive, and tell us the format and quantity. The minimum is 100 stickers, production is 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free proof, and FedEx shipping in the United States is free. The rest of what we print is listed on the Die Cut Stickers home page.

faqs.q: Are custom waterproof stickers dishwasher safe?
faqs.a: Yes, on the top rack. Laminated vinyl on a steel or glass bottle takes repeated cycles without lifting or fading. Daily washing for months will eventually dull a gloss laminate, so choose matte if the item is washed every day, and let the sticker set 24 hours before its first wash.

faqs.q: What makes a sticker waterproof rather than just water-resistant?
faqs.a: Three things together: a film base (vinyl or BOPP) that cannot absorb water, inks cured on the surface, and a laminate sealed over the print and edges. Water-resistant stickers skip the laminate or use coated paper, so they handle splashes but not soaking or scrubbing.

faqs.q: How do you print waterproof stickers so the ink does not run?
faqs.a: The ink is printed onto vinyl or BOPP film and cured, then a clear laminate is pressed over the whole sheet before cutting. The laminate, not the ink, faces the water. A home inkjet print on paper or unlaminated film will bleed, which is why that route rarely works.

faqs.q: Will waterproof stickers stay on a plastic cooler or kayak?
faqs.a: Yes, with permanent adhesive and a clean surface. Polyethylene coolers and kayaks are low-energy plastics, so wipe them with rubbing alcohol, apply the sticker dry, press firmly and give it 24 hours before it goes near water. Keep the sticker on a flat or gently curved area.

faqs.q: Can waterproof stickers be printed on clear film with no white background?
faqs.a: Yes. Clear vinyl or clear BOPP shows only the printed art once applied, which suits bottles and glass where you want the surface to show through. Light colors need a white ink layer underneath or they vanish; we show that layer on the proof so you can check it.

faqs.q: How many custom waterproof stickers do I have to order?
faqs.a: 100 stickers per design is the minimum. Prices start at $0.30 per sticker, set by size, quantity and whether you choose white or clear film, and fall as the run grows. Several designs can share one order so a product line hits the minimum together.

faqs.q: Do waterproof stickers hold up to sweat and sunscreen on sports gear?
faqs.a: Sweat and water, yes, indefinitely. Sunscreen and insect repellent are solvents that haze a laminate over a season of heavy use, so rinse gear when you can. On helmets, bottles and bike frames the stickers hold for years; on soft silicone bands and rubber grips the adhesive will not bond.

faqs.q: Can I order waterproof stickers on a roll for a labeling machine?
faqs.a: Yes. Roll labels come wound on a 3" core with the unwind direction and gap set to your applicator, and they carry the same vinyl or BOPP stock and laminate as our singles. Tell us the machine model at quoting and the roll spec is matched on the proof.

faqs.q: Will a waterproof sticker survive the freezer?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as it is applied at room temperature and allowed to set before freezing. The film and laminate are unaffected by cold, and the adhesive keeps its bond once formed. Applying a sticker to an already frozen surface is the mistake to avoid, since the adhesive will not grab.

faqs.q: Are all weather stickers the same as waterproof stickers?
faqs.a: Not quite. Waterproof covers water, soap, sweat and dishwashers, with a life of 3 to 5 years indoors or sheltered. All-weather adds years of direct sun, frost and heat, using a thicker outdoor vinyl and UV laminate. For a truck, sign or mailbox, order the outdoor grade.

faqs.q: Can waterproof stickers come off a bottle without leaving residue?
faqs.a: With removable adhesive, yes, from glass, steel and smooth plastic: warm the sticker, peel slowly from a corner, and wipe any faint tack off with soapy water. Permanent adhesive is built to stay and will leave residue that needs rubbing alcohol, so pick removable if the item will be relabeled.

faqs.q: How long do custom waterproof decals keep their color?
faqs.a: Indoors or on gear stored out of direct sun, 3 to 5 years before any visible fading. In daily full sun, a standard laminate softens after 2 to 3 years, which is where the outdoor grade with a UV laminate earns its price. Matte and gloss laminate age at about the same rate.
